39K views · 589 reactions | LaGrange council denies data center permit 

Hogansville council extends moratorium 

By Jennifer Shrader
BeeTV33 staff report 

For as fast as the Google data center appeared to move in to LaGrange and Troup County, projects since then are comparatively moving from the speed of fiber internet to a party line phone. 

LaGrange City Council voted Tuesday night to deny a special use permit for a data center on Pegasus Parkway and Old Hutchinson Mill Road — a project that would have been in an industrial area but also would have abutted residential properties not in the city limit.

The LaGrange council had taken a large amount of criticism from the local anti-data center coalition when, on the verge of approving an ordinance regulating data centers this spring, they appeared to balk on a comprehensive measure and instead decided to require each center to apply for its own special use permit. 

Tuesday night was the first test of that decision. 

Before the vote, council took comments from residents of the city and county for nearly an hour, including two families that would be in between the Google data center on Pegasus Parkway and the one being proposed. 

Patricia Schramm, a resident of rural Troup County, doesn’t live near either project but does live directly across the street from a Hyundai plant, a Kia supplier built on Webb-Bartley Road that was annexed into West Point. She told LaGrange council she has lost her well, her driveway and foundation are cracked, and there is constant air and noise pollution. 

“I am a victim of poor planning,” she said, telling the council they have the same power as a small group to ruin the rural character of the area, along with the lives of residents.

She concluded with a 10-second recording of the plant’s generators running—a noise she says she hears all day on Sunday. 

One of the data center opponents’ main concerns is the generators they will have, for the noise and air pollution. 

No one spoke in favor of the data center permit aside from the developer’s attorney, who didn’t answer questions raised by several of the residents who spoke against the proposal. 

Also on Tuesday, Hogansville City Council voted to extend the city’s moratorium on data centers another 90 days, to Dec. 7. The action comes after council failed to pass a data center ordinance at its last meeting, after months of work and two public hearings. The city will go back to work on the ordinance, which will mean residents will have at least one more public hearing to voice their concerns. 

The extension puts a proposed data center at the city’s former sewage sprayfield, which is also surrounded by rural county land, on hold. 

No data center projects have come to the Troup County Commission, which passed a restrictive ordinance earlier this year essentially guaranteeing any data center would have to be annexed into the city of LaGrange. | BEETV
